Coler Preserve in Bentonville, Arkansas, is a prime example of this: a paved trail extends less than a mile from the vehicular parking area to a beautiful modernist coffee shop seamlessly nestled in the hillside where visitors can relax and congregate around, and even on top of the shop. Signature destinations throughout the system are primed for access by bike, foot, or even floating, rather than relying solely on vehicular parking. Appropriate amenities to secure bicycles, canoes, or kayaks should be provided at these locations. Strategize Progressive Amenities The MPCA should feature world-class recreation opportunities connected by world class trails, complemented by equally renowned supporting amenities. Bicycle storage should feature covers for protection from the elements, and floating piers at launch points should have identifiable areas to secure watercraft. Fix-it stations for bicycles should be at access points as well as in select remote trail segments to prevent users becoming stranded. Striving for immersive experiences in nature can coexist with broadband technology by incorporating hotspots at remote trailheads for safety purposes. Ideally, a comprehensive MPCA user application would provide in-depth detail as to the nearest amenities pertaining to their selected recreation types, such as docks for floating and fishing, or water fountains for a backpacker or hiker. FITNESS In October, Jim Dailey Fitness and Aquatic Center introduced a new Pilates class. Pilates is a low-impact exercise method focused on strengthening muscles while improving postural alignment and flexibility. Developed by Joseph Pilates in the early 20th century, it emphasizes core strength, controlled movements, and mindful breathing. Classes typically involve a series of mat exercises or equipment-based workouts, targeting various muscle groups. Pilates is suitable for individuals of all fitness levels and can enhance overall body awareness, stability, and balance, making it a popular choice for those seeking a holistic approach to fitness., which is held on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:00 PM. On-site visitation included 759 walk-in guests and 2,101 visitors to special events, tours, etc. during the month. Fair K-8 Preparatory Academy through the 21st Century program. Hot dogs and chips were provided by Home Instead and Pinnacle Legacy Law. Bluebell Creameries and Central Arkansas Water provided ice cream and water. Other museums participating in the event this year were the Old State House Museum, Mosaic Templars Cultural Center, the Museum of Discover, Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts, Firehouse Museum and Hostel, Historic Arkansas Museum, and the Witt Stephens Nature Center. Our Youth & Teen Swim Fit class is designed to help young swimmers, ages 10 through 17, develop their swimming skills while improving strength, endurance, and overall fitness. This high-energy class is perfect for those looking to enhance their technique, work on their stamina, and build confidence in the water. Participants will focus on all four competitive strokes—freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly—while also incorporating conditioning exercises to improve cardiovascular health, flexibility, and muscular strength. Whether your swimmer is preparing for competition or simply wants to stay active and fit, Swim Fit provides a supportive and fun environment to achieve personal goals and boost athletic performance. The class attracted a total of 78 attendees for the month. The 6 aquatic classes at Jim Dailey Fitness and Aquatic Center are performing exceptionally well. SPECIAL ACTIVITY For the month of November, Baptist Health Community Outreach conducted a monthly blood pressure checks for our members and visitors, with a total of 16 individuals taking advantage of these services. 4 The Centre at University Park The month of November was a great start to finishing the year out with a bang. Starting out with gearing up for a new year, the procurement team came into the month with training classes and open enrollment kicked off with an awesome start with 66 staff members taking care of their benefits for 2025. What a way to begin the month and seeing the staff here at The Centre pull together as a team to make everything a smoother process is even better. We had our regular meetings such as NUSA, Age Friendly and Work Order. Most of all it was wonderful hosting the Parks STAT this month, seeing 48 of our directors, leaders and overseers was great to witness. We had fun, food and fellowship while taking care of and covering business. The building is continuously being beautified and kept up; we got fresh mulch put down it’s making the building stand out even more than before. We continue to grow and put our best foot forward here at The Centre at University Park. Youth Athletics Youth Basketball Season is the next activity, registration is going on at each location, the goal is to have at least 350 youth registered. They have also done skills & drills and are now into their team practices. Games sites will be determined later due to ongoing facility renovations. Registration is still open for cheerleading and basketball. Kudos to all the staff at all centers for continuing to ensure everything is running smoothly. Adult Athletics Interstate Park Program Field Rental reservations have stayed steady for the youth football league requesting ball field rentals with lights. Adult Softball Program Interstate Adult softball has ended for fall ball and registration for the spring league will begin January 15, 2025, for Men, women, coed and church league. Summer Playground Program We are working on making the summer playground program more enjoyable for the summer of 2025. First Tee Golf Is it summer or is it winter? Some days feel like summer some days, others feel like winter but as we keep a close eye on temperatures rising and dropping throughout the day and night, the leaves continue to fall on the golf course. This keeps our staff busy this time of year, keeping the golf course leave-free so golfers can have an enjoyable experience at our facility while playing the game of golf that they love without the risk of losing golf balls. Although we think this time of year would be slow, the warmer days have been keeping us busy, which is great for revenue. One of our goals for 2024 was to make over $300,000 in revenue. We were able to reach that goal the second week in November. The increase in revenue has been continuing to fluctuate between 11% and 12 1/2% for the last three months, which means we are on a great path of growth and rounds for the year. We were able to use the rest of the funding that was donated by the Jewish community for our historical site on the property. If you have not had a chance to look at this site, you should. Not only is it a wonderful piece of Arkansas history but it also involves golf. On Veterans Day, we did twilight rates all day long and to show our appreciation to veterans, all veterans got to pay for free that day. As we start to get into the colder months of the holiday season, the grass is slowly starting to go dormant. This does not slow down the golfers as they come out and enjoy and play the game that they love. If you have not been to First Tee lately, I invite you to come out and check out the facility. Check out the golf course or stop in and say “Hi”. Our staff is always here to greet you and to make you feel like you’re at home. Rebsamen Golf We had over 60 ladies in attendance for our weekly lady’s day for the month of November, it will be lower 5 since the weather is cooling down. Revenue for 2024 is still up 5% over 2023. Nike products has been approved to be ordered and will be stocked for 2025, in the pro shop. May have to cover greens sooner than normal, if the temperatures continue to fall and get to freezing. Looking to hire more staff in the beginning of the year. Rebsamen Tennis USTA League Combo State tournament Nov 1-2 (150 players). Monday night Rebsamen Doubles league finished its 25th year in November (will start again in March). Monday night Rebsamen Singles league still going through end of year (10-12 courts each week). Thursday night Rebsamen Doubles league finishes early December (1-2 courts, continuing to build). Raul and Janan fall junior development groups going strong and are year-round. Hired four new part time tennis aide positions, excited to have them on board. Working on filling out the 2025 tournament and league schedules. MacArthur Museum of Arkansas Military History Museum attendance for November was 2,327. This total includes: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) off-site programming and outreach. On-site visitation included 475 walk-in guests and 463 visitors to special events, tours, during the month. In addition to Arkansas, visitors came from 24 states: Alabama, California, Colorado, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and Washington as well as from South Korea and the Netherlands. The museum's virtual documentaries/interviews received 319 new views through November 25 for a total of 5,406 views for 2024. Off-site programming included 79 youth and parents at the “Corvettes and Veterans” outreach on November 10 at War Memorial Stadium. Total attendance for the first eleven months of 2024 is 40,656. Museum staff continues to present off-site programming to children at Dunbar and Stephens Community Centers as part of the museum’s After School program. During November,195 children received instruction through this weekly outreach. The museum has raised $30,852 thus far in 2024, surpassing its goal of raising $30,000 each year in donations, grants, and sponsorships with one month remaining in the year. Gift shop sales thus far in 2024 are approximately $10,272. The museum worked with the MacArthur Park Group to host a public reception to unveil the five finalists in the design competition for a new shade structure for the MacArthur Unleashed dog park. A total of 106 persons attended the event during which a winning design was selected by those present. The winner was a design submitted by AMR Architects. The group will work with the Parks Department to raised funds for the shade structure. Attendance for the November 19 “Movies at MacArthur” film Elvis and the USS Arizona was 62. Attendance for the film program this year is 627, breaking last year’s record attendance of 517. Staff unveiled the schedule for the 2025 season at the event which is also posted on the museum website. https://www.littlerock.gov/residents/parks-and-recreation/directory/macarthur-museum-of-arkansasmilitary-history/upcoming-events/2025-movies-at-macarthur/ The museum hosted the Captain and crew members of USS Arkansas, a new Virginia-class submarine currently under construction in Newport News, VA, on November 8. The crew participated in interviews and a press conference at the museum. The November 9 issue of the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette featured an article on the event, which was also covered by Channels 4 and 16 news. A link is listed below. Vessel’s captain drops by in state The museum participated in the second annual “Corvettes and Veterans” show at War Memorial Stadium on November 10. Museum staff joined with other local exhibitors to showcase the museum’s programs as well as military memorabilia. Approximately 79 people visited the museum table to learn more about programming and exhibits. The museum continues to host Two Minutes to Midnight and the Architecture of Armageddon, a traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA and Mid-America Arts Alliance in Kansas City, MO. The exhibit examines the atomic age and Cold War through two photographic essays that look at the offensive and defensive implications of nuclear war. It includes 40 photographic images and will remain through January 5, 2025. A historical marker commemorating the contributions of African American soldiers in the Civil War is scheduled for production this month at Sewah Studios in Marietta, Ohio. Once the marker has 6 been received the museum will coordinate its installation on the parade grounds behind the museum with a presentation by Mark Christ on the United States Colored Troops (USCT). The marker and a bench for the parade grounds behind the museum were both funded by David F. Gruenewald in memory of his father Felix Gruenewald. Outdoor Recreation Weekly Mountain bike and road bike rides have continued but attendance has decreased due to cooler temperatures and Day Light Savings. I will be transitioning to Saturday Road rides, once or twice a month and biweekly mountain bike rides. The November Disc Golf Pop-up at War Memorial on 11/24/24 was held in conjunction with a food drive to benefit Parks & Rec's Seniors programs. Prep work and planning for the Squatch Till You Drop trail running event took several weeks and involved: Course layout and marking, arranging for MEMS, securing donations (lunch was donated and prepared by the non-profit Central Arkansas Trail Alliance), monitoring and finalizing participant registrations, posting public notices signs and social media notices, securing volunteers (we had 15 volunteers who logged over 60 hours), coordinating Day-of set-up and other last minute details. It was a busy time but well worth it. The November 16th, “Squatch TIll You Drop” trail running event had 75 participants and was covered by Channel 7 and the Democrat Gazette. A survey was sent to all participants and the responses were all very positive. To date, the even raised over $3,500 in revenue.
